scope: Milestone B on-device verification of the Android companion client: the agent stage (AgentSession + terminal renderer + composer + history paging) exercised live on the phone's cover screen through the ADB loopback harness, with a Mac-side WireSession attached to the same services to prove both clients stay in sync.

verified_commits.app: 0719ec7 (feat: stage a live agent on the Android client)
verified_commits.harness: 69ac9fd (feat: add an ADB control harness for the Android client)

device.hardware: Samsung Z Fold SM-F966U over USB, debug APK (dev.lapis.remote)
device.display: Cover display active for all runs: display 0 at 1080x2520, state ON; inner display 1 at 1968x2184, state OFF (device folded). Milestone B's finish line names the cover screen.
device.transport: adb reverse tcp:7351 to the fixture gateway; the gateway runs with --allow-local so the loopback peer is admitted. No overlay membership is exercised by this gate.

harness.recipe: Disposable fake_agent services (echo/second/parked) registered in a temp workspace, apps/remote/lapis_remote.py bound to 127.0.0.1:7351 with --allow-local and a tailscale fixture, reached from the phone through adb reverse; a MacClient WireSession attaches as a second viewer. The app is driven through tools/qa/android_ctl.py (uiautomator node tree, taps, text injection) and asserts on the terminal's accessibility description, mirroring the iOS harness's accessibilityValue reads.
harness.teardown: The script tears down services, gateway, and the adb reverse tunnel unless --keep is passed.

checks.list: Workspace screen lists the fixture agents by category
checks.open: Agent stage opens and streams; first frames render
checks.sync: Text typed on the phone reaches the agent; the Mac-side session observes the phone's ping and its pong renders on the phone (mac_saw_phone true)
checks.draft: A typed draft without Enter stays pending on the prompt line and is preserved through composer interaction; the check then clears and submits the draft so later checks start from a clean prompt
checks.scrollback: count fixture pages history; scrolling up loads older rows and the numbered content is readable in the accessibility description
checks.resize: App-driven layout and a wm size override both re-grid the agent; frames report 56x50, 56x52 and 37x27 grids from an initial 100x30
checks.background: App backgrounded and returned without losing the stream or the terminal view; the Mac side never retired the phone's view (mac_closed_by null)
checks.crash: Process-liveness and dropbox crash scan clean at the end of the run

result.receipt: build/android/remote-check.json: checks [list, open, sync, draft, scrollback, resize, background, crash], failed [], mac_saw_phone true, mac_closed_by null, grids [100x30, 37x27, 56x50, 56x52]
result.runs: Full suite green twice: once on the instrumented diagnostic build during root-causing and once on the final clean build; unit checks 67/67 in scripts/check_android.py and 12/12 in scripts/tests/test_android_ctl.py
result.screens: ignored build/android/remote-screens/<run>/ (workspace, stage, sync, draft, scrollback, resize, background steps); screenshots contain fixture terminal content only and are not committed

defects_found_and_fixed: Terminal accessibility text was a plain field read inside the Compose semantics block, so same-line edits (an agent overwriting its own prompt line) reached the accessibility tree only when a scroll or structural change invalidated the node. TalkBack and uiautomator reads were stale while rendering was correct. Fixed by making the history cache's accessible text snapshot state (0719ec7); semantics now re-apply on every change.
limitations: The live agent is the fake_agent fixture (deterministic PTY program), not a real Codex CLI; it rides the same service/PTY/SSE path, and server-side verification against a real Codex TUI is recorded in evidence/android-milestone-b-server.json. The on-device real-CLI run is folded into the milestone A/D overlay gates so it exercises the production transport rather than adb reverse.
Transport is the adb-reverse loopback, not Tailscale/ZeroTier; overlay admission on the device is milestone A/D's gate (phone has not joined the private network).
All runs were on the cover display; fold/unfold re-grid behavior is milestone D's gate.
Input was injected text (paste semantics) rather than the soft keyboard's IME path; IME composition on Android is not yet exercised.
